calls.head: The Wild are likely to drive the play
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Wild have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Sharks one of the worst. The ice is likely to tilt the Wild’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

SJS.head: We gave San Jose only a 36% chance, and it went the way we feared.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 64% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Minnesota couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: San Jose usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Minnesota’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.6% against San Jose) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

surprises.head: Minnesota brought the hits
surprises.body: Minnesota’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 183, against their usual 106 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

surprises.head: Minnesota’s power play feasted on San Jose’s kill
surprises.body: San Jose has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: Minnesota’s power play created 14.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.8 (about 8.7 against San Jose) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 15 games.

story.head: Four points for Kaprizov as the Wild beat the Sharks
paras: It was a busy first period. Kirill Kaprizov opened the scoring for the Wild on the power play early in the period. Tyler Toffoli tied it 1-1 for San Jose on the power play just over three minutes later. Alexander Wennberg put the Sharks ahead 2-1 late in the first, but Brock Faber made it 2-2 for Minnesota with 42 seconds left in the period. Joel Eriksson Ek put the Wild ahead 3-2 just 13 seconds into the second. Blake Coleman added the empty-netter with less than two minutes left to make it 4-2, and Eriksson Ek struck again into the empty net with just under a minute left. Kaprizov finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Eriksson Ek added an assist for a three-point night.

The Wild had the better of the chances, outshooting the Sharks 31-24. Filip Gustavsson shook off a shaky start for the Wild, allowing two goals on the first eight shots and none on the last 16, and Yaroslav Askarov stopped 26 of 29 at the other end. The Wild moved to 18-3-5, still first in the NHL in points, while the Sharks dropped to 11-13-2, third in the Pacific.
